mathcounts-potw-2026-04-06-01.title: Scale factor
mathcounts-potw-2026-04-06-01.body:
The model is $\frac{9.5}{1450}$ of real size. $4000 \times \frac{9.5}{1450} = \frac{38{,}000}{1450} \approx 26.21$ ft.

**Answer: 26.2 feet**

mathcounts-potw-2026-04-06-02.title: Find 1% first
mathcounts-potw-2026-04-06-02.body:
1% of 71,000,000 is 710,000 lb, so 0.01% is 7,100 lb. 21,600 lb is about $21{,}600 \div 7{,}100 \approx 3.04$ hundredths of a percent, i.e. $0.03\%$.

**Answer: 0.03%**

mathcounts-potw-2026-04-06-03.title: Convert time to hours
mathcounts-potw-2026-04-06-03.body:
50 min $= \frac56$ h, so the time is $3\frac56 = \frac{23}{6}$ h. Speed $= 216 \div \frac{23}{6} = \frac{1296}{23} \approx 56.3 \approx 56$ mph.

**Answer: 56 mph**

mathcounts-potw-2026-04-06-03.title: Miles per minute
mathcounts-potw-2026-04-06-03.body:
Time $= 230$ minutes. $216 \div 230 \approx 0.939$ miles per minute, times 60 $\approx 56.3$ mph.

**Answer: 56 mph**

mathcounts-potw-2026-04-06-04.title: Divide
mathcounts-potw-2026-04-06-04.body:
$40{,}000{,}000 \div 15 \approx 2{,}666{,}667$ visitors, which is about 2,667,000 to the nearest thousand.

**Answer: 2,667,000**

mathcounts-potw-2026-04-06-04.title: Thousands of visitors
mathcounts-potw-2026-04-06-04.body:
Each 1000 visitors pay \$15,000 toward construction. $40{,}000{,}000 \div 15{,}000 \approx 2666.7$ thousand visitors $\approx 2{,}667{,}000$.

**Answer: 2,667,000**
